clue.text: Sterilise parts - i.e. use after treatment

indicators.note: something that has undergone treatment has been processed and changed, so the preceding letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter, ignoring the dash

explanation.surface: An instruction to sterilise some components, apparently, once they have been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: To pasteurise milk is to heat it to kill germs, a partial form of sterilising it.

clue.text: Route used by bellhop at hotel

indicators.note: the answer is put to use inside the words that follow, lying within their letters

blocks.note: the end of bellhop, all of at and the start of hotel

explanation.surface: The way a hotel porter takes through the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a way or track taken from one place to another, so it is a synonym of route.

clue.text: Volume so staggering around large oil terminal

indicators.note: something staggering lurches unsteadily, so these letters lose their order
around says the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the next piece

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A huge amount of oil reeling around a big terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sullom Voe is the big oil terminal in Shetland, the islands off the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullom Voe in the Shetland Islands is one of Europe's largest oil and gas terminals, handling North Sea crude.

clue.text: Flightless bird from upper region men unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled describes things disturbed from their place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly, coming from where men in high country feel unsettled.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor penguin of Antarctica is the largest penguin species, and penguins cannot fly.

clue.text: Acknowledged Republican committed perjury

blocks.note: Rep. is a common abbreviation for Republican
perjury is lying under oath

explanation.surface: A US Republican admitted to having lied under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acknowledged' reads as the politician admitting something, but it is the definition, in the sense of answering a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge a message is to respond to it, so acknowledged and replied are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Caretaker in bar before opening

blocks.note: to bar something is to stop it
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A janitor standing in a pub before it opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker' suggests a janitor; here it is the temporary sense, as in a caretaker government.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker manager or government fills in temporarily, which is exactly what a stopgap does.

clue.text: Sign of an injury received by Francesca recently

indicators.note: the answer is taken in and held by the words that follow, sitting within their letters

blocks.note: the end of Francesca plus the first letter of recently

explanation.surface: Francesca bears the mark of a wound she picked up lately.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on the skin after a wound has healed, so it shows an injury.

clue.text: Set of beliefs about inner ring

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, Latin for about
in archery the inner is the red ring next to the gold centre of a target
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A creed concerning an exclusive clique of insiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner ring' reads as a clique, but the two words split: inner is an archery term for the red ring of a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, Latin for I believe, is a creed or statement of the principles someone holds.

clue.text: Firm decision about suspension

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
in chemistry a suspension or solution is a substance dispersed in a liquid

explanation.surface: A definite ruling on whether someone should be suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolution is a firm resolve or determination to do something, such as a New Year's pledge.

clue.text: Question one girl about revolutionary dish

blocks.note: qu. is a standard abbreviation for question
the Roman numeral for one
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Interrogating a young woman about a radical's food.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in a different order from the clue: about loosely places the girl next to the revolutionary, after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiche Lorraine is a savoury open tart of egg, cream and bacon, a classic French dish.

clue.text: Helpful hint about extremely unusual bulb

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters only
about says the hint goes around the following letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: a tip is a useful piece of advice
the first and last letters of unusual

explanation.surface: Advice about an especially rare plant bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for unusual, but it takes only the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips grow from bulbs, and gardeners call the planted bulb by the flower's name.

clue.text: Impresarios, awfully crude when surrounded by professionals

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are thrown out of order
the jumbled word is enclosed, with the following word wrapped around it

blocks.note: taken as written
pros is short for professionals

explanation.surface: Showbiz managers who turn very vulgar when in the company of experts.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios organise and finance shows, which is the job of a theatrical or film producer.

clue.text: Getting on train for Greyfriars, say

blocks.note: getting on a train or bus is boarding it
to train someone is to school them

explanation.surface: Catching a train to go to Greyfriars at the start of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway; it is the verb meaning to teach. Greyfriars is the fictional school of Billy Bunter in Frank Richards's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyfriars, home of Billy Bunter, is a fictional English school where pupils live in, an example of the type.

clue.text: One should guarantee payment from reportedly Bohemian character

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the next word is to be taken by its sound

blocks.note: Bohemia is part of the Czech Republic
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: Getting a promise of payment from an artistic free spirit, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' suggests an unconventional artist; it means someone from Bohemia, now in the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque guarantee card, once issued by British banks, promised that the bank would honour a cheque up to a set limit.

clue.text: He drove recklessly and was suspended

indicators.note: recklessly suggests wild, uncontrolled movement, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A dangerous driver who was then banned from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was suspended' suggests a driving ban; it is the definition meaning hung in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hovered hung in the air without moving, which is to be suspended.

clue.text: Clown making most of mistake in mine

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped
in places the shortened word inside the following one

blocks.note: first part of pit, a mine
error without its last letter
last part of pit, a mine

explanation.surface: A circus clown botching things in a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime and commedia dell'arte.

clue.text: Contrite, salesman over upset tenant

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rep is short for sales representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sorry salesman standing over a distressed tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue over means placed on top, so the salesman comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contrite feels sorry for a wrong, which is to be repentant.

clue.text: Sounds like signal at college to form a line

indicators.note: sounds like says the next word is to be replaced by one spoken the same way

blocks.note: a cue is a signal to begin, as for an actor
a student at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: An instruction at college telling students to line up.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to Oxford or Cambridge and are up while there.
explanation.definitionFit: To queue up is to wait one behind another, standing in a line.

clue.text: Point me out allspice

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A request to have the allspice pointed out in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is another name for allspice, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree used as seasoning.

clue.text: Sign of arachnid with no tail

indicators.note: with no tail means the end of the word is cut off, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: a scorpion is an arachnid

explanation.surface: Evidence of a scorpion that has lost its stinging tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A scorpion's tail carries its sting, which makes the surface vivid; the sign is the zodiac kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, represented by the scorpion.

clue.text: Genuine note subsequently placed on top

blocks.note: since means subsequently, and placed on top puts it above the next piece in this down entry
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An authentic note later stuck on top of a pile.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere feelings are honest and real, which is what genuine means.

clue.text: A promising band?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pop group with a bright future
setter's reading: a ring of metal given as a pledge to marry

explanation.walkthrough: Band reads as a group of musicians and promising as talented; in fact band is a ring and promising means making a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring given when a couple agree to wed is a band worn to signal that promise of marriage.

clue.text: One staring open-mouthed, Greek primate inside

indicators.note: inside places the primate within the abbreviation that comes before it

blocks.note: first half of GR, the abbreviation for Greek
an ape is a primate
second half of GR, the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: A Greek gawping at a monkey in an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare with the mouth wide open, so a gaper is someone doing so.

clue.text: Try to find out

blocks.note: first meaning: a judge tries a case in court
second meaning: learn of news

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction to investigate; the two halves are separate meanings, the legal one of judging a case and the everyday one of learning news.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hears a case when it tries it, and to hear news is to learn of it.

clue.text: Place a pin nervously in device

indicators.note: doing something nervously means fumbling, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Anxiously putting a pin into a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or piece of equipment, often a domestic one like a toaster.

clue.text: Picture that is printed in supplement? On the contrary

indicators.note: printed in says one item is set within another, as text sits inside a publication
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the holder and the held trade places

blocks.note: first half of ie, short for id est, that is
a newspaper supplement is often a magazine, mag for short
second half of ie

explanation.surface: A photo that appears in a newspaper's colour supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: As written, ie goes inside the magazine; on the contrary reverses that, putting the magazine inside ie. 'That' does double duty, opening ie.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness, such as a photograph.

clue.text: Daughter approaching ship in little or no light

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
Noah's ark was a ship

explanation.surface: A daughter nearing a vessel at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is dark is one in which there is little or no light.

clue.text: O?

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclamation, or a lone circle
setter's reading: the letter O stands for nil, which in tennis scoring is called love

explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a score of zero is love, and zero looks like O, so O is the letter that means love.
explanation.definitionFit: A love letter is normally a romantic message; here the phrase is read literally as the character standing for love.
